Benchmark Stage 3 detection speed at several worker counts

Source: R/birdnet_benchmark.R
pam_birdnet_benchmark.Rd

Runs pam_detect() on the same random sample of recordings once per worker count and reports throughput, scaling efficiency, and an estimate for the whole archive. Use it to choose birdnet$workers for your CPU, and as the baseline to compare the new backend against.

Usage

pam_birdnet_benchmark(
  cfg,
  workers = c(1L, 2L, 4L, 8L),
  n_files = 8L,
  seed = 1L,
  keep_runs = FALSE
)

Arguments

cfg

A pam_config object.

workers

Integer vector of worker counts to test. Counts above the number of logical cores are dropped with a warning.

n_files

Files per run. Each file takes about a minute for a 60-minute recording, so keep this small (default 8).

seed

Seed for the file sample, identical for every run.

keep_runs

If FALSE (default) the temporary detection folders are deleted afterwards.

Value

A data.frame with one row per worker count: workers, n_done, n_failed, elapsed_s, files_per_hour, speedup, efficiency and est_hours_full. Also written to <logs>/birdnet_benchmark.csv.

Details

The timing includes model loading in every worker, which is part of the real cost of starting a run. Real runs amortise it over many files, so the full-archive estimate is slightly pessimistic. Run on an otherwise idle machine.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cfg <- pam_load_config("config.yml")
pam_birdnet_benchmark(cfg, workers = c(1, 4, 8), n_files = 8)
} # }
